summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her third cycle of high-dose methotrexate for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CNS involvement. She tolerated the chemotherapy well and cleared the drug within 48 hours. During the admission, she developed abdominal pain and increased ostomy output, prompting imaging and stool studies. A CT scan showed bowel wall edema and pneumatosis, and a stool test confirmed Clostridium difficile infection, for which she was treated with oral vancomycin. Her symptoms resolved by discharge. Her diabetes was managed with insulin due to elevated blood sugars in the hospital, though she was not discharged on insulin due to hypoglycemia risk. She received IVIG for CVID and completed a dose of Neupogen to support white blood cell recovery. She was discharged home with follow-up arranged and instructions to complete her vancomycin course.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Other malignant lymphomas, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
